title: access-evidence-and-siem-pipeline-compact-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic playbook for mapping customer questionnaire requests to minimal evidence artifacts, and for preparing our SIEM export pipeline so we can deliver example payloads during assessments. Intended audience: product security, solutions engineering, and CS engineers handling security questionnaires (esp. fintech/reg customers).

Context and constraints:
- Customers frequently ask for small-bite evidence during sales cycles: ‘show me an audit log sample with RBAC events’ or ‘what fields do you send to the SIEM’.
- We must avoid sharing production PII or exact timestamps; provide synthetic but realistic samples, and document the transformation and retention policies.
- This doc is intentionally compact; it complements the longer evidence workbook. Use it for quick turnarounds and embed links to canonical artifacts.

Quick mapping (question -> short-evidence deliverable):
- Who can view/download customer data? -> RBAC role matrix CSV + policy link + exported role-change audit sample (anonymized).
- How are access changes logged? -> Audit log schema snippet + example event sequence (role assignment, token issuance, session termination).
- Can we demonstrate SIEM export? -> Export mapping doc + sample JSON export for common SIEM fields.
- Retention and deletion proof? -> Retention policy excerpt + data deletion job run log (redacted).

Audit log schema (minimal recommended view for customers):
- event_id: uuid (string)
- occurred_at: iso8601 (string, timezone-aware)
- tenant_id: string (redacted for sample as tenant: T-XXXX)
- user_id: string (hashed id in shared sample)
- actor_type: {user, service, system} (string)
- action: string (e.g., role.assign, role.revoke, token.issue, token.revoke, model.infer.start)
- object_type: string (role, token, model, dataset)
- object_id: string (redacted)
- outcome: {success, failure} (string)
- ip_address: string (obfuscated)
- user_agent: string
- request_id: string
- meta: free-form map (we flatten key:value in SIEM exports)

Notes: When we share a sample, we replace tenant_id/user_id/object_id with stable synthetic ids, and we shift all timestamps into a fixed window (e.g., 2023-06-01T10:00:00Z + offsets) to preserve event ordering without leaking real timing.

SIEM export adapter — practical transformation guidance:
- Input: internal audit log events (see schema above).
- Output: flattened JSON lines (NDJSON) where meta.* keys are promoted: e.g., meta.role_name -> role_name.
- Field renames we use for customer-facing exports: tenant_id -> customer_tag, user_id -> actor_hash, occurred_at -> event_time.
- PII handling: ip_address -> ip_range (first two octets), user_agent -> ua_family (chrome/firefox/other) unless explicit consent granted.
- Compression/packaging: deliver NDJSON gzipped with a per-file manifest that lists included event types and timestamp window.

Sample SIEM NDJSON line (synthetic):
{
  "event_time": "2023-06-01T10:00:12Z",
  "event_id": "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-abcdef000001",
  "customer_tag": "T-XXXX",
  "actor_hash": "user-hash-7a9f",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "action": "role.assign",
  "object_type": "role",
  "role_name": "billing-admin",
  "outcome": "success",
  "ip_range": "54.23.x.x",
  "ua_family": "chrome",
  "request_id": "req-97f0"
}

Checklist for quick-turn responses:
- [ ] Confirm scope of requested evidence (which tenants, which time window, export size limit).
- [ ] Pull synthetic sample via script (scripts/prepare-siem-sample.sh) and validate redaction rules.
- [ ] Attach retention policy excerpt + link to Confluence canonical policy.
- [ ] If RBAC question: attach role matrix CSV and a human-readable row showing role -> permissions mapping.
- [ ] Run a brief privacy review (owner: product-security) before sending.

Messaging snippets for customer emails (short):
- "Attached is a small, redacted sample of our audit events and a short description of how we export to SIEMs. Let me know if you want a tailored export for your ingest schema and we can coordinate a short technical call."

Open items / unresolved questions:
- Do we have an approved canonical obfuscation library? (current: ad-hoc scripts under github.com/redwood-inference/siem-adapter — PR #42 is WIP).
- Should we include an example showing model.infer.latency events for latency SLA conversations? (pros: helpful; cons: might reveal perf patterns).
- Standardize the manifest format across dedicated/private customers vs hosted.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marco: final PR for obfuscation-helper library (jira:SEC-2193) -> ETA 2024-10-10.
- Sofia: prepare role-matrix template for CS (csv + markdown explainer) -> ETA 2024-09-30.
- Evelyn: script to generate time-shifted synthetic samples (scripts/prepare-siem-sample.sh) -> ETA 2024-10-07.

Notes to self (E.P.):
- Keep samples deliberately small (<=500 events) for sales proofs.
- For on-prem/private customers, prefer a live demo of SIEM forwarder instead of static samples.

References (internal):
- Confluence: SECURITY-ONBOARD-5678 (canonical retention policy)
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/siem-adapter (adapter + obfuscation scripts)
- Jira: SEC-2193 (obfuscation helper work)

History / revision log:
- 2024-02-14: initial draft (Evelyn).
- 2024-03-02: added SIEM flat-mapping and sample event (Marco).
- 2024-10-03: updated delivery checklist, action items, and owners (Evelyn).

If you're triaging a questionnaire and need to move fast: start here, pick the smallest set of deliverables that answer the ask, and escalate to engineering only if the customer needs a custom export format.
